info.summary: A complete, replayable logical solution to one Sudoku puzzle. The file is a JSON array: element 0 is this header plus the full initial board; elements 1..N are the solve steps in order, each performing exactly one action. Everything needed to render and explain the solve is in this file — no prose parsing is required to recover any value.

conventions.cell_labels: A cell is the string 'r3c7' — 1-indexed, row then column. Every cell reference in this file, at any depth (including inside 'extra'), uses this form.
conventions.digits: Digits are 1-9. A 0 means an empty cell, and appears only in the header's 'puzzle' grid.
conventions.versioning: Read schema_version. A major bump may break consumers; a minor bump only adds fields. Treat unknown fields as additive and ignore them.

header_fields.step: Always 0. Identifies this element as the header.
header_fields.schema_version: Version of this format, e.g. '1.1'. Check the major before consuming; minor bumps are additive only.
header_fields.info: This block: a self-contained description of the file format.
header_fields.strategy: Always null on the header (present so every element has the same shape).
header_fields.puzzle_id: Puzzle number within its generation run, or null.
header_fields.difficulty: Overall grade band of the puzzle: easy | medium | hard.
header_fields.points: Sum of every step's score contribution (raw difficulty).
header_fields.highest_strategy: The hardest strategy the solve needed.
header_fields.clue_count: Number of givens in the puzzle.
header_fields.puzzle: The starting grid as 9 rows of 9 ints; 0 = empty cell.
header_fields.solution: The completed grid as 9 rows of 9 ints, or null if the writer was not given one.
header_fields.step_count: Number of elements after this one.
header_fields.move_count: Number of distinct strategy applications (see info.moves).
header_fields.strategy_counts: Map of strategy id to how many steps it produced.
header_fields.legend: Map of cell role to {color, meaning}. See info.roles.
header_fields.strategy_primers: Map of strategy id to a beginner primer {name, what, why, spot, terms?}. Held once here rather than repeated on every step. Only covers strategies this puzzle actually uses.
header_fields.cells: All 81 cells of the initial board. role and highlight are null.

step_fields.step: 1-based sequential index of this atomic action.
step_fields.move_id: Which strategy application this action came from. Steps sharing a move_id were produced by one move. See info.moves.
step_fields.move_index: 1-based position of this action within its move.
step_fields.move_size: Total number of actions in this move.
step_fields.pattern_state_step: The step whose board state the pattern fields describe (always the move's first step). See info.moves — this matters for correctness.
step_fields.strategy_label: Display name, e.g. 'X-Cycle'. Use this rather than deriving from strategy: title-casing mangles acronyms ('Als Xz').
step_fields.difficulty: Difficulty band of this strategy. See info.difficulty_bands.
step_fields.explanation: Player-facing prose {observation, logic, action, result}, safe to render as-is. See info.explanation.
step_fields.action: The single board change this step makes. See info.action_types. This is the only field that mutates state; see info.replay.
step_fields.unit: The unit the pattern lives in, e.g. 'row 3', or null.
step_fields.candidate_set: The pattern's candidate set, e.g. [2,8] for a naked pair.
step_fields.focus_cell: The cell being changed; same as action.cell.
step_fields.elimination_cells: Every cell this move removes a candidate from.
step_fields.pivot_cell: Wing / ALS pivot cell, or null.
step_fields.fin_cells: Fin cells of a finned fish.
step_fields.chain_cells: Chain cells, in path order where the chain is a path. See info.chains.
step_fields.cells: Board snapshot of only the cells involved in this step, after the action was applied. See info.cells and info.replay.

explanation.observation: What the board currently shows.
explanation.logic: Why this pattern forces the action.
explanation.result: What changed on the board.

cell_fields.value: Confirmed digit 1-9, or 0 if the cell is still empty.
cell_fields.candidates: Remaining candidate digits; empty when value != 0.
cell_fields.role: Semantic role of this cell in the step. Drive colour from this.
cell_fields.highlight: Legacy colour name (new_placed | eliminated | pattern). Prefer 'role'.

action_types.place: Write action.digit into action.cell as its confirmed value.

difficulty_bands.diabolical: Almost Locked Sets and forcing chains.

roles.description: Each cell in a step has exactly one role, resolved by the first match in role_priority. 'legend' maps each role to a suggested colour and meaning.
roles.accessibility: Colour alone is not sufficient — roles should also be conveyed by shape, pattern or a text badge.

chains.description: chain_links describes the inference chain edge by edge, so it can be drawn rather than only asserted in prose. Each edge is {from, to, type, digit, unit, unit_type}.

link_types.strong: The named unit has ONLY these two homes left for the digit, so one of them must be it. Suggested rendering: solid line.
link_types.weak: The two cells share the named unit, so they cannot BOTH be the digit (but neither is guaranteed). Suggested rendering: dashed line.

by_strategy.x_cycle: A closed loop. Edges strictly alternate starting with a weak link, and the last edge returns to chain_cells[0]. A discontinuous loop closes with a weak edge (that flaw is what forces the elimination); a continuous loop closes strong. See extra.cycle_type.
by_strategy.xy_chain: A path. Every edge is weak and carries the digit shared by two bi-value cells. chain_cells is in path order, so numbering the cells is meaningful.
by_strategy.simple_colouring: A TREE, not a path: every edge is strong, and the edges are not a walk along chain_cells — do not number them. Use extra.colour_a and extra.colour_b to paint the two alternating groups; that distinction is the strategy.

moves.description: One strategy application can produce several atomic actions — a Simple Colouring that clears a whole colour emits one step per removed candidate. Steps from the same application share a move_id.
moves.why_it_matters: The pattern fields (chain_links, pattern_cells, support_cells, ...) describe the board as it was when the strategy fired: the step named by pattern_state_step, which is the move's first step. Later actions in the same move may already have altered the cells the pattern is built from — Simple Colouring Rule 1 eliminates its own chain cells, so by action 2 the chain no longer holds on the board being displayed.
safe_rendering: Render all actions of a move as one frame (recommended for chain strategies) so the pattern and the board agree.
Or step through actions individually, but only draw pattern overlays when step == pattern_state_step.

extra.description: Strategy-specific detail, exported verbatim so no value has to be recovered from prose. Cells inside use the same 'r3c7' labels. Treat as open: new keys may appear within a minor version.

always_present.candidates_before: Candidates on the board before the move — the scoring factor.

replay.description: The header's 'cells' holds the full starting board. Each step's 'cells' holds only the cells involved in that step, so a renderer carries board state forward itself by applying each step's 'action' in order.
replay.propagation: After a 'place', removing that digit from the cell's peers is IMPLIED — it is not emitted as separate steps. A peer is any cell sharing the row, column or box.
replay.guarantee: Applying every action in order yields the completed grid, which matches the header's 'solution'.

description: Initial puzzle

focus.meaning: The cell being solved or changed

fin.meaning: Fin cells of a finned fish

naked_single.name: Naked Single
naked_single.what: A cell where eight of the nine digits have already been ruled out, leaving exactly one candidate.
naked_single.why: A cell must hold some digit. If every digit but one is already used by a cell in the same row, column or box, the survivor is the only legal choice.
naked_single.spot: Scan for cells showing a single pencil mark. After every digit you place, re-check its row, column and box — placements often cascade.

hidden_single.name: Hidden Single
hidden_single.what: A digit that still has to go somewhere in a unit, and only one empty cell in that unit can still take it.
hidden_single.why: Every unit must contain all nine digits exactly once. If a digit is blocked out of every cell of the unit but one, it is forced into that cell — even if the cell has other candidates too.
hidden_single.spot: Pick a digit and a unit, then cross out every cell of the unit that already sees that digit. One survivor means a placement.

terms.unit: A row, a column, or a 3x3 box — the three groups that must each hold the digits 1-9 exactly once.

naked_pair.name: Naked Pair
naked_pair.what: Two cells in the same unit whose candidates are the same two digits, and nothing else.
naked_pair.why: Those two digits have to fill those two cells in one order or the other. Either way both digits are used up inside the pair, so no other cell of the unit can take them.
naked_pair.spot: Look for two cells in one unit showing an identical pair of pencil marks, then sweep the rest of that unit for those digits.

pointing_pair.name: Pointing Pair / Triple
pointing_pair.what: Inside one box, every remaining spot for a digit happens to sit on a single row or column.
pointing_pair.why: The box must contain the digit somewhere, and all its options are on that one line — so the digit is guaranteed to land on that line inside the box. The rest of the line, outside the box, therefore cannot use it.
pointing_pair.spot: Take a box and a digit, and check whether all its candidates share a row or a column. If so, follow that line out of the box.

box_line_reduction.name: Box/Line Reduction
box_line_reduction.what: The mirror image of a pointing pair: within one row or column, every remaining spot for a digit sits inside a single box.
box_line_reduction.why: The line must contain the digit, and all its options fall in one box — so the digit is guaranteed to land inside that box on that line. The rest of the box therefore cannot use it.
box_line_reduction.spot: Take a line and a digit, and check whether all its candidates fall in one box. If so, clear that digit from the box's other cells.
